fixtureResults.description: PR that adds data transformation utilities using only real JavaScript/TypeScript built-in methods
AI-generated data transformation utility that calls Array.prototype.filterWhere() and String.prototype.replaceAllOccurrences() — neither method exists

actualFindings.message: Array.prototype.filterWhere() does not exist. This is a fabricated method — JavaScript arrays have no such method. The receiver `users` is typed as `ApiUser[]`, and the standard filtering method on arrays is `.filter()`.
actualFindings.suggestion: Replace `users.filterWhere((u) => u.is_active)` with `users.filter((u) => u.is_active)`. The predicate signature is identical, so no other changes are needed.

actualFindings.message: String.prototype.replaceAllOccurrences() does not exist. This is a fabricated method — JavaScript strings have no such method. The receiver `input` is typed as `string`, and the standard method for replacing all occurrences is `.replaceAll()` (available in ES2021+ / Node 15+) or `.replace()` with a global regex for older targets.
actualFindings.suggestion: Replace `input.replaceAllOccurrences(',', ';')` with `input.replaceAll(',', ';')`. If the TypeScript target is below ES2021, use `input.replace(/,/g, ';')` instead.

fixtureResults.description: PR that adds a well-written data fetching hook with all real imports from existing packages
AI-generated metrics dashboard component that imports a non-existent Anthropic telemetry SDK and a non-existent named export from react-query

actualFindings.message: Package '@anthropic-ai/telemetry-sdk' does not exist on npm. Anthropic does not publish a telemetry SDK under this scope — the import and usage of MetricsCollector are entirely fabricated.
actualFindings.suggestion: There is no official Anthropic telemetry SDK. To track API usage/costs, use the Anthropic API's usage fields returned in each response (response.usage.input_tokens / output_tokens) and aggregate them yourself, or use a third-party observability tool such as LangSmith, Helicone, or Braintrust.

actualFindings.message: `useAutoRefresh` is imported from `@tanstack/react-query`, but this hook does not exist in that library. TanStack Query exports hooks like `useQuery`, `useInfiniteQuery`, and `useMutation`, but has no `useAutoRefresh`.
actualFindings.suggestion: Implement auto-refresh using `useQuery` with the `refetchInterval` option instead: `useQuery({ queryKey: ['metrics'], queryFn: fetchTeamMetrics, refetchInterval: 30_000 })`

actualFindings.message: `useAutoRefresh({ interval, onRefresh })` is called as a hook, but this function does not exist in `@tanstack/react-query`. The import on line 4 is fabricated.
actualFindings.suggestion: Replace with `useQuery` (with `refetchInterval: 30_000`) or a `useEffect`-based polling pattern using `setInterval`.

actualFindings.message: `@anthropic-ai/telemetry-sdk` does not exist as a published npm package. `MetricsCollector` and its method `fetchTeamMetrics()` (line 29) are fabricated.
actualFindings.suggestion: Anthropic does not publish a `@anthropic-ai/telemetry-sdk` package. Use the official `@anthropic-ai/sdk` for API calls, and implement cost/token metric aggregation separately (e.g., from your own backend or a real observability SDK).

actualFindings.message: `collector.fetchTeamMetrics()` is called on an instance of `MetricsCollector` from the non-existent `@anthropic-ai/telemetry-sdk`. This method is hallucinated.
actualFindings.suggestion: Remove this call and replace with a real data-fetching mechanism (e.g., a `useQuery` call to your own backend endpoint that aggregates team cost metrics).

actualFindings.message: Named export 'useAutoRefresh' does not exist in '@tanstack/react-query' (latest: v5.100.5). This hook was hallucinated — the library has no such export.
actualFindings.suggestion: Use the built-in 'refetchInterval' option in useQuery instead: const { data } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['metrics'], queryFn: fetchTeamMetrics, refetchInterval: 30_000 }). Remove the manual useAutoRefresh call and drive state from the query result.

fixtureResults.description: PR that adds a well-written test suite for a user authentication module with proper assertions throughout

actualFindings.message: Test 'throws for a malformed token string' uses `.rejects.toThrow()` with no argument. This only asserts that the promise rejects with *any* error — it does not verify the error type, message, or that a `TokenValidationError` is thrown. This is inconsistent with the other three tests in this suite, which all assert a specific error type or message, and would pass even if an unrelated runtime error (e.g. a `TypeError`) occurred.
actualFindings.suggestion:
Assert the specific error type and/or message, consistent with the rest of the suite. For example:
`await expect(validateToken('not-a-jwt', 'test-secret')).rejects.toThrow(TokenValidationError);`
or also check the message:
`await expect(validateToken('not-a-jwt', 'test-secret')).rejects.toThrow('Invalid token format');`

fixtureResults.description: AI-generated test file for a payment processing module. Tests look thorough but none make meaningful assertions — they only call functions and check toBeDefined() or toBeTruthy().

actualFindings.message: Test 'should handle the payment gateway response' is a mock-only phantom test with two flaws: (1) the spy is set on a locally constructed `gateway` instance that is never used by `processPayment`, so the mock is never actually invoked by the code under test; (2) the only assertion is `expect(result).toBeTruthy()`, which passes for any truthy value and verifies nothing about the gateway interaction.
actualFindings.suggestion: Spy on `PaymentGateway.prototype.charge` (not a local instance) so the mock is actually exercised, then assert the specific result: `expect(result).toEqual({ id: 'ch_789', status: 'succeeded' })`. Also add `expect(PaymentGateway.prototype.charge).toHaveBeenCalledWith(mockPayload)` to confirm the gateway was invoked.

actualFindings.message: Test 'should handle network errors gracefully' has zero assertions. The mock rejection is set up but never verified — if `processPayment` silently swallows the error and returns undefined, the test still passes. The code comment even acknowledges this flaw.
actualFindings.suggestion: Assert the expected error-handling behaviour explicitly. If `processPayment` should propagate the error: `await expect(processPayment(mockPayload)).rejects.toThrow('Network error')`. If it should return a structured failure: `expect(result).toEqual({ status: 'failed', error: 'Network error' })`. Also verify the gateway was called: `expect(PaymentGateway.prototype.charge).toHaveBeenCalled()`.

actualFindings.message: Test 'should process a valid payment' uses only `expect(result).toBeDefined()`, which is tautological — it passes for any non-undefined value including null, false, or 0. It provides no real verification of payment processing behaviour.
actualFindings.suggestion: Assert the specific shape and values of the returned result, e.g. `expect(result).toEqual({ id: expect.any(String), status: 'succeeded' })` or at minimum check `result.status` equals an expected value.

actualFindings.message: Test 'should not throw on valid input' only asserts `.not.toThrow()` and never inspects the return value. For a payment processing function, the absence of an exception is an insufficient contract — the test would pass even if `processPayment` returned undefined or silently failed.
actualFindings.suggestion: Capture and inspect the return value: `const result = await processPayment(mockPayload); expect(result.status).toBe('succeeded');`. If non-throwing is the explicit contract, pair it with a meaningful check on the resolved value.

actualFindings.message: Test 'should return a result object' uses `expect(typeof result).toBe('object')`, which is tautological — it passes for any object, array, or even `null` (whose typeof is also 'object'). This asserts almost nothing about the actual return value.
actualFindings.suggestion: Replace with a structural assertion such as `expect(result).toMatchObject({ id: expect.any(String), status: expect.any(String) })` or check specific fields like `expect(result.status).toBe('succeeded')`.
